data.gender_notes: Rabbi is used as a male name in christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The meaning of Rabbi is recorded in name-lists as “My teacher”. This meaning has NOT been verified against a classical lexical or onomastic source, so it is published as an unverified candidate only. The record is flagged for manual source verification.
data.spiritual_meaning: Rabbi expresses “My teacher”; spiritual readings of the name are interpretive.
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rabbi total 23, reducing to 5. Number 5 is associated with freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_hebrew.name: רַבִי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: From the Hebrew word רב (rav) meaning 'great' or 'master'. In the context of religious teachers, it came to mean 'my great one' or 'my master'. It's also a title of respect for elders or leaders.

in_greek.name: ραββί
in_greek.long_meaning: From the Aramaic word רבי (rabbi) which was adopted in Greek. It's equivalent to the Greek word διδάσκαλος (didaskalos) meaning 'teacher'.

in_latin.name: Rabbi
in_latin.long_meaning: Adopted directly from the Greek ραββί (rabbi) and the Hebrew רב (rav). It's equivalent to the Latin word magister or doctor, meaning 'teacher' or 'master'.

biblical_reference.note: The title Rabbi is used in the Hebrew Bible to refer to respected elders, teachers, and leaders. In the New Testament, it's used to refer to Jesus' disciples and other religious teachers.
